name: kobai-project
// exports: This Project is not a library and nothing imports from it, but `src/migration-set.ts` resolves its own `migrations/` directory by asking Node where this manifest is — which Node only allows a package to do for itself when the manifest names something in `exports`. The alternative was counting `..` segments, which is wrong at one of the two depths this code runs at. See the comment in that file.
// scripts: Every command this Project has. It shipped a `devbox.json` until ADR-0083: a Developer owns this repository outright (ADR-0001), and a scaffolder that bakes a tool into the artifact makes that tool a dependency of running your own store. Node and Docker are the whole of what this needs. There is deliberately no `install` script — `pnpm install` is the command, and a script by that name is an npm lifecycle hook that would run during it.

scripts.// up: Postgres and this Project, built and running. The one command a first run needs: Core applies its migrations at boot, so there is no separate migration step and no half-set-up state to reason about.
scripts.// db: Just Postgres, for running the app on this machine with `pnpm run dev`.
scripts.// build: Both halves, and naming them is load-bearing. This Project is the root of its own two-package workspace and `pnpm -r` skips the root, so a command that only walked the workspace would build the Admin, report success, and leave this Project's own TypeScript uncompiled — the first symptom being `node dist/src/server.js` saying the file does not exist. It used to be `pnpm -r --include-workspace-root build`, which said the same thing in a flag whose absence was silent; that shape cannot survive here, because a root script named `build` running `pnpm -r --include-workspace-root build` would call itself. Naming the Admin and this Project's own compile says it outright and cannot recurse.
scripts.// typecheck: Both halves, for the same reason `build` names both.
scripts.// dev: `--env-file-if-exists=.env` reads this Project's own `.env`, which is where `.env.example` tells a Developer to put one. It builds first so `/admin-ui` serves something; `pnpm run admin:dev` is what to run when the Admin is the thing being edited.
scripts.// admin:dev: The Admin with a reload loop, in a second terminal beside `pnpm run dev`. A Vite dev server proxying /admin, /store and /health to the app, so the browser still sees exactly one origin — which is what production looks like and why there is no CORS configured anywhere (ADR-0010, ADR-0033).
scripts.// db:generate: This Project owns tables of its own, so it generates migrations of its own — the same `drizzle-kit generate` Core and every Plugin run, against this Project's own schema and into this Project's own `migrations/`. `tablesFilter` in drizzle.config.ts keeps a generate here from ever writing a migration that touches Core's tables or a Plugin's.
scripts.// db:push: There is deliberately no db:push script here either. A Project's database holds Core's tables, every wired Plugin's, and its own, so `drizzle-kit push` — which diffs against the LIVE database — reports success while silently dropping the tables of whichever packages the pushed schema does not know about, and leaves their tracking rows behind so the migration runner cannot repair it. Generate a migration instead. See ADR-0030, https://github.com/y3owk1n/kobai/blob/main/docs/adr/0030-generate-and-migrate-only-never-drizzle-kit-push.md

// dependencies: `kobai-project-admin` is a dependency rather than a devDependency because this process serves its `dist` at runtime — `src/admin-assets.ts` finds it through Node's own module resolution, which is right whether this file runs from `src` or from `dist`. Everything that *builds* the Admin is a devDependency of that package, so the built assets are all the runtime needs.
// devDependencies: `drizzle-kit` is what `db:generate` runs, and it is a dev dependency for the same reason it is one in Core and in the Plugin: generating a migration is something a Developer does at their desk, and applying one is something Core does at boot through `drizzle-orm`. The container needs the second and not the first.
